(1976 Code § 7.12.070) 4-4-5: INFLAMMABLE RUBBISH; ACID AND EXPLOSIVES: No person shall place or cause to be placed in or near the receptacle provided for the removal of ashes any highly inflammable rubbish, acids or explosives of any kind whatsoever. (1976 Code § 7.12.080) 4-4-6: PENALTY: Any person violating a provision of this chapter shall, upon complaint and conviction thereof, be subject to fine as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 7.12.100; amd. 2016 Code) 4-4-7: DISPOSAL OR DUMPING OF REFUSE OTHER THAN BRANCHES AND GRASS CLIPPINGS: A. Intent to Adopt Policy: It is the intent of the Town of Terry to implement a policy to protect the Town's dumping area for branches and grass clippings. B. Policy: Effective as of the 8th day of August, 2020, it shall be in violation of this Section to dump anything other than branches and/or grass clippings. C. Violation of Policy: Upon the first offense, any person found to have violated this Section shall be subjected to retrieval of the items, and pay for any costs incurred in that retrieval. Upon the second or subsequent offense, the Town shall impose of fine of two hundred dollars ($200.00), retrieval the items, and pay for any costs incurred in the retrieval. If a person is found guilty of a violation under this part, fails to pay any penalty under section A above, the penalty and the cost of abatement shall be assessed against the person's taxes. (Ord. 2020-02, 7- 13-2020) **TITLE 5** **PUBLIC SAFETY** **CHAPTER 1** **LAW ENFORCEMENT** SECTION: 5-1-1: Law Enforcement Contracted With County 5-1-1: LAW ENFORCEMENT CONTRACTED WITH COUNTY: Pursuant to an intergovernmental agreement, the town has contracted with the Prairie County sheriff's department to enforce state statutes and county and town ordinances, including, but not limited to, traffic enforcement and criminal and civil enforcement. (2016 Code) **CHAPTER 2** **FIRE DEPARTMENT** SECTION: 5-2-1: Composition 5-2-2: Officers Of Department 5-2-3: Fire Chief, Powers And Duties 5-2-4: Assistant Chief 5-2-5: Command At Fires 5-2-6: Fire Limits 5-2-7: Ordering Business Near Fire Closed 5-2-8: Preventive Inspections 5-2-9: Hazardous Obstructions; Orders To Remove Or Remedy 5-2-10: Obstructing Personnel Or Equipment 5-2-11: Penalty 5-2-1: COMPOSITION: The fire department of the town shall consist of a chief of the fire department, assistant chief of the fire department, and such firefighters as may be authorized by the bylaws of the volunteer fire department. (1976 Code § 2.24.010) 5-2-2: OFFICERS OF DEPARTMENT: The volunteer fire department of the town shall elect the officers and directors of the fire department, and shall follow all applicable laws of the state regarding the operation of a volunteer fire department. (1976 Code § 2.24.020) 5-2-3: FIRE CHIEF, POWERS AND DUTIES: The chief of the fire department shall have sole command and control over all persons connected with the fire department of the town, and shall possess full power and authority over its organization, government, and discipline, and to that end may, from time to time, establish such disciplinary rules and regulations as he may deem advisable, subject to the approval of the town council; he shall have charge of and be responsible for the engines and other apparatus, the property of the town furnished the fire department and see that they are at all times ready for use in the extinguishing of fires. (1976 Code § 2.24.030; amd. 2016 Code) 5-2-4: ASSISTANT CHIEF: In the absence of the chief of the fire department, the assistant chief of the department shall exercise the functions and powers set forth in section 5-2-3 of this chapter. (1976 Code § 2.24.040) 5-2-5: COMMAND AT FIRES: A. Fire Chief: The chief of the fire department, or the officer having charge in his place, shall have sole and absolute control and command over all other members of the fire department and all other persons present at fires, and the movement of all persons or property within the streets in any area threatened by fire. (1976 Code § 2.24.050) B. First Member Or Officer On Scene: The firefighter or officer of the fire department who first arrives at a fire shall be the officer in command until the chief or assistant chief of the fire department arrives. (1976 Code § 2.24.060) 5-2-6: FIRE LIMITS: The fire limits shall be and are hereby declared to be within the limits of the town, according to the plat thereof on file in the Prairie County Courthouse. (1976 Code § 2.24.140) 5-2-7: ORDERING BUSINESS NEAR FIRE CLOSED: A. The chief of the fire department shall have power, during any fire, and while the fire department is engaged in putting out any fire or caring for property at any fire, to order any place of business in the vicinity of such fire closed for such length of time as he determines necessary for the safety and preservation of life and property. B. Any person who violates an order made pursuant to this section shall be punished as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 2.24.080) 5-2-8: PREVENTIVE INSPECTIONS: It shall be the duty of the chief of the fire department to inspect or cause to be inspected, as often as may be necessary, all buildings, premises and thoroughfares in the town, except the interior of private dwellings, for the purpose of ascertaining and causing to be corrected, any conditions liable to cause fire, or any violations of the provisions of this code or other ordinance of the town affecting fire hazards. (1976 Code § 2.24.090) 5-2-9: HAZARDOUS OBSTRUCTIONS; ORDERS TO REMOVE OR REMEDY: A. Removal Of Obstructions; Orders: Whenever the chief of the fire department, or any officer of the town or firefighter shall find obstructions to or on fire escapes, stairs, passageways, doors, windows, etc., liable to interfere with the operations of the fire department, or egress of the occupants in case of fire, he shall order the same to be removed or remedied. (1976 Code § 2.24.100) B. Compliance Required: Orders issued under authority of subsection A of this section shall be complied with promptly by the owner, his agent, or occupant of the building or premises involved. Any person failing to so comply shall be punished as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 2.24.110) 5-2-10: OBSTRUCTING PERSONNEL OR EQUIPMENT: A. Fire Personnel: It shall be unlawful for any person to in any way interfere with or hinder any firefighter while in the discharge or apparent discharge of his duty of preventing fire. (1976 Code § 2.24.120) B. Fire Equipment: No person having in his charge or under his control any automobile, motorcycle, motor truck, or motor vehicle of any kind shall drive or in any way cause or allow the same to pass over and upon any hose belonging to the town while such hose for any purpose whatever may be placed upon any of the streets, alleys, or in any place whatever in the corporate limits of the town, unless at a point where such hose may, at the time, be securely bridged. (1976 Code § 2.24.130; amd. 2016 Code) 5-2-11: PENALTY: Any person violating a provision of this chapter for which another penalty has not been provided shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 2.24.150) **CHAPTER 3**

laws.title: Storage of Explosives or Flammable Liquids
laws.content:
**A. Explosives:** It is unlawful for any person to keep or permit to be kept, any giant powder, nitroglycerin, dynamite, or other highly explosive compound within the Town or within three (3) miles of the corporate limits of the Town. (1976 Code § 9.08.030)

**B. Flammable Liquids:**

1. It is unlawful for any person to store flammable liquids in outside aboveground tanks within the corporate limits of the Town.

2. No person within the Town shall store flammable or combustible liquids or liquefied petroleum gas in new bulk plants. (1976 Code § 9.08.040; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: Fireworks
laws.content:
**A. Discharge Restricted:** The discharge, firing or use of firecrackers, rockets, torpedoes, roman candles, or other fireworks or substances designed or intended for pyrotechnic display or demonstration, within the Town, is prohibited before July 3 and after July 5 and before and after December 31. (1976 Code § 9.08.050; amd. 2016 Code)

**B. Selling Restricted:** It is unlawful for any person to offer for sale, expose for sale or sell at retail or wholesale, within the corporate limits of the Town, any fireworks of any nature whatsoever, before June 24 and after July 5 and before December 29 and after December 31. (1976 Code § 9.08.060; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: Swimming Pools, Illegally Entering
laws.content: It is unlawful for any person to climb into or break into, or enter, the swimming pool of the Town during the hours when not open to public use; and any person convicted of breaking into, climbing into, or illegally entering said swimming pool area during such hours when not open shall be subject to fine as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this Code, and shall pay for all damages to the premises. (1976 Code § 9.20.010; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: Penalty
laws.content: Any person violating a provision of this chapter for which another penalty has not been provided shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this Code. (1976 Code § 9.08.070)

laws.title: Camping
laws.content:
**A. Definitions:** For purposes of this section, to camp means:

1. To erect a tent or shelter of natural or synthetic material, prepare a sleeping bag or other bedding material for use, or park a motor vehicle, motor home, or trailer for the apparent purpose of overnight occupancy;

2. To sleep at any time between the hours of eleven o’clock (11:00) P.M. and six o’clock (6:00) A.M. outdoors, with or without bedding, sleeping bag, blanket, mattress, tent, hammock, or other similar protection;

3. To sleep at any time between the hours of eleven o’clock (11:00) P.M. and six o’clock (6:00) A.M. in, on, or under any structure or object, any motor vehicle, motor home, or trailer, with or without bedding, sleeping bag, blanket, mattress, tent, hammock, or other similar protection; or

4. To establish or maintain outdoors or in, on, or under any structure or thing not intended for human occupancy, at any time between the hours of eleven o’clock (11:00) P.M. and six o’clock (6:00) A.M., a temporary or permanent place for sleeping, by setting up any bedding, sleeping bag, blanket, mattress, tent, hammock, or other sleeping equipment or device or setting up any cooking equipment with the intent to remain in that location overnight.

**B. Camping Prohibited:** It shall be unlawful for any person to camp in any public park, or on any publicly or privately owned property within the Town limits with the exception of designated camping areas, whether State, County, Town, or privately owned, and with appropriate authorization; or on private property with the authorization of the property owner.

**C. Violation A Misdemeanor; Penalty:** Any person violating any provisions of this section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine not to exceed five hundred dollars ($500.00), or imprisonment for a term not to exceed six (6) months, or both. (Ord. 2017-01, 4-20-2017)

laws.title: Disturbing the Peace
laws.content: No person within the town, or within three (3) miles of the town limits, shall wilfully and maliciously disturb the peace and quiet of any street, neighborhood, family, or person by loud, tumultuous noise, or by tumultuous or offensive conduct, or by using offensively loud radio or television sets, or by threatening, quarreling, scolding, hallooing, hollering, uttering obscene, profane, vulgar, or indecent language in the presence of any person or persons, challenging to fight, or fighting, or by cursing, swearing, or by committing any obscene, vulgar, indecent, or lewd act in any public place, or in view of any person or persons. (1976 Code § 9.16.010)

laws.title: Vagrancy
laws.content:
The following persons shall be deemed guilty of committing the crime of vagrancy:

A. Every person begging food, money, drinks, lodging or other things, or soliciting charity for himself or dependents.

B. Every person who lodges in or about any marketplace, shed, railroad car, outhouse, lavatory, rest room, warehouse, barn, service station, school, bar, cocktail lounge, or any other place of business or structure within the town, without the permission of the owner or party entitled to possession thereof. (1976 Code § 9.16.020)

laws.title: Open Containers
laws.content:
A. Public Ways: It shall be unlawful for any person to carry, possess, or drink alcoholic beverages, beer or ale, in open containers on any public street or alley in the town. Any person convicted of carrying, possessing or drinking alcoholic beverages, beer or ale in open containers, on any public street or alley in the town shall be subject to fine as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code.

B. Murn Park: It shall be unlawful for any person to carry, possess, or drink alcoholic beverages, beer or ale, in open containers, within the limits of Murn Park, located on blocks five (5) and twelve (12) of the original townsite of Terry, Montana, between the hours of ten o’clock (10:00) P.M. and eight o’clock (8:00) A.M. Any person convicted of carrying, possessing, or drinking, alcoholic beverages, beer or ale, in open containers, within the limits of Murn Park in the town between the hours of ten o’clock (10:00) P.M. and eight o’clock (8:00) A.M. shall be subject to fine as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 9.16.030; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: Weapons
laws.content:
A. Shooting Of Firearms:

1. The shooting of all firearms, or weapons, including rifles, pistols and shotguns in the town, or at the town dump, town sewage lagoon or other property under the control of the town, outside of the town limits is hereby prohibited. (1976 Code § 9.24.010)

2. Any person violating this subsection A, whether in the town, or at property under the control of the town, but outside the corporate limits thereof, shall be punished by a fine as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code, together with the costs of prosecution.

B. Shooting Air Rifle Or BB Gun: Every person who wilfully shoots or fires off any air rifle or BB gun within the limits of the town is guilty of a misdemeanor and punishable by a fine not exceeding twenty five dollars ($25.00) and such air rifle or BB gun shall be seized and impounded by a law enforcement officer until satisfied that the fine; if any, will be paid or that the violations of this subsection will cease. Thereafter said air rifle or BB gun shall be returned to the owner. (1976 Code § 9.24.010; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: Penalty
laws.content: Any person violating a provision of this chapter for which another penalty has not been provided shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 9.16.050)

laws.title: Curfew
laws.content:
A. Age And Hour Restrictions: It is unlawful for any person under the age of eighteen (18) to remain in or upon any of the streets, alleys or public places in the corporate limits of the town after the hours of ten o’clock (10:00) P.M. of any day from September 1 to the following May 1 of any year, and from May 1 to August 31 inclusive of each year, after the hour of eleven o’clock (11:00) P.M., except Friday and Saturday nights until one o’clock (1:00) A.M., unless such person is accompanied by a parent, guardian or other person having the legal custody of such minor person; or unless such minor person is performing an errand or duty directed by such parent, guardian or other person having the legal custody of such minor; or unless the minor’s employment makes it necessary for him, or her, to be upon such streets, alleys, or other places during the nighttime after the specified hours. B. Responsibility Of Parents: It is unlawful for any parent, guardian or other person having the legal custody of any person under the age of eighteen (18) years to allow or permit such minor, while in such legal custody, to be in or upon any of the streets, alleys or public places in the town within the times prohibited in subsection A of this section, unless there exists a necessity thereof. (1976 Code § 9.16.040) C. Penalty: Any person violating the provisions of this section shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 9.16.050)
**CHAPTER 5** **ANIMAL CONTROL**
SECTION: 5-5-1: Definitions 5-5-2: License Required; Exceptions 5-5-3: Registration And Vaccination Required 5-5-4: Tag And Collar 5-5-5: Dog Kennel License 5-5-6: Cruelty To Animals 5-5-7: Nuisance Animals 5-5-8: Vicious Animals 5-5-9: Investigation 5-5-10: Interference With Law Enforcement Officer 5-5-11: Dogs Running At Large 5-5-12: Animals Exposed To Rabies 5-5-13: Impoundment, Redemption And Disposition Of Animals 5-5-14: Prevention Of Rabies 5-5-15: Penalty 5-5-1: DEFINITIONS: As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise indicated: AT LARGE: Shall be intended to mean off the premises of the owner, and not under the control of the owner or a member of his immediate family or a person authorized by the owner, either by leash, cord, chain or otherwise. CONTROL: Shall be intended to mean controlled by a leash, of a length of no greater than ten feet (10') held by a person physically capable of controlling the dog on such leash, or within the limits of the premises controlled by the owner or other persons consenting thereto, or inside a vehicle or other enclosure controlled by the owner or other persons consenting thereto. DOG: Shall be intended to mean both male and female; either or neither, from date of birth thereafter. KENNEL: Any premises or property of any kind or description where more than two (2) female dogs are kept for breeding purposes, or where more than one litter of pups or dogs are kept for purposes of sale. OWNER: Shall be intended to mean any person or persons, firm, association, partnership, corporation, or other legal entity owning, keeping or harboring a dog. VACCINATE: The inoculation of a dog or other animal with an antirabies vaccine by any licensed veterinarian. (1976 Code § 8.04.010; amd. 2016 Code) 5-5-2: LICENSE REQUIRED, EXCEPTIONS: A. License Required: In the event a dog is brought within the town within the license (calendar) year, the owner or person having possession or custody of or harboring or giving shelter or refuge to such dog shall obtain a license for such dog as provided in this chapter. B. Exceptions: The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to any person visiting the district for a period not exceeding thirty (30) days, and owning, having possession or custody of or harboring or giving shelter to a dog currently licensed and bearing a license issued by another licensing authority. It shall be unlawful to have possession or custody of or to harbor or give shelter or refuge to any dog without a valid dog license. (1976 Code § 8.04.170) 5-5-3: REGISTRATION AND VACCINATION REQUIRED: A. Registration And Vaccination; Fee: 1. All dogs kept, harbored or maintained in the town shall be vaccinated and registered as herein provided on or before March 1 of each year. Registration tags shall be issued by the town clerk upon proof of vaccination for rabies within a two (2) year period immediately upon payment of a registration fee of ten dollars ($10.00) per year for every dog, except as provided in subsection B of this section. Should said license fee not be paid on or before March 1 annually, then said license fee shall be deemed delinquent and in the event that the license fee hereby levied becomes delinquent, the license agent shall cause to be levied and collected, in addition to the license fee herein set forth, a ten dollar ($10.00) delinquent fee. 2. The owner shall state at the time of application for registration and upon printed forms provided for such purpose, his name, address and the name, breed, color, and sex of each dog owned or kept by him. 3. Proof of vaccination shall consist of a certificate of vaccination from a registered, licensed, and practicing veterinarian. (1976 Code § 8.04.110) B. Lower Fee For Persons Over Sixty: The registration fee for a dog owned by a person over the age of sixty (60) years, shall be the sum of five dollars ($5.00) per dog, and must be paid on or before March 1 of each year. In the event the registration fee becomes delinquent according to the provisions of subsection A of this section, the regular registration fee and delinquent fee shall apply. (1976 Code § 8.04.110; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: TAG and Collar
laws.content:
A. License Issuance:

1. Upon payment of the registration fee as provided in section 5-5-3 of this chapter, the license agent shall issue to the owner a registration certificate and a metallic tag for each dog so registered. The shape of the tag shall be changed every year and shall have stamped thereon the year for which it was issued and a number corresponding with the number of the certificate.

2. The town clerk shall be the license agent and may appoint additional license agents as he or she may deem necessary to be expedient. (1976 Code § 8.04.040)

B. Collar; Tag Attached: Every owner shall provide his or her dog with a collar to which the license tag must be affixed and the owner shall be responsible to see that the collar and tag are constantly worn. In case the tag is lost or destroyed, a duplicate will be issued by the license agent upon payment of a fee of one dollar ($1.00). The license tags shall not be transferable from one dog to another. (1976 Code § 8.04.040; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: DOG Kennel License
laws.content: Any person maintaining a "kennel" as defined in section 5-5-1 of this chapter shall pay a license fee of twenty five dollars ($25.00) per year for maintaining such kennel. No license shall be issued until the premises to be used for the kennel has been inspected and approved by the Prairie County health officer. (1976 Code § 8.04.050; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: Cruelty to Animals
laws.content: It is unlawful for any person to wilfully and cruelly inflict pain upon or injure any animal. (1976 Code § 8.04.060)

laws.title: Nuisance Animals
laws.content:
A. It is hereby declared a public nuisance for any dog or other animal to destroy property or other pets; to bite or chase after persons not trespassing on the property of, or injuring or attempting to injure the person, family or property of the owner; to chase vehicles in public streets or ways; or by prolonged howling, yelping, barking or by any other means, cause annoyance or disturbance to any person. (1976 Code § 8.04.070)

B. Any such nuisance animal may be taken up and impounded by any law enforcement officer.

C. It is unlawful for any person to own, harbor, keep or maintain any such nuisance animal and it shall be the duty of any law enforcement officer to issue tickets and file complaints for all such violations occurring in their presence.

D. Any person aggrieved by a nuisance animal may file a complaint with a law enforcement officer to be investigated for potential charges for a potential violation of this section where the offense is not committed in the presence of any law enforcement officer.

E. Upon a third conviction under this section, the nuisance animal shall be seized and taken up by any law enforcement officer and put to death forthwith. (1976 Code § 8.04.070; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: Vicious Animals
laws.content:
A. Definition: The term "vicious animal" shall mean:

1. Any dog or other animal, while off the owner's property and in the absence of intentional provocation, chases or approaches any person in a menacing fashion or apparent attitude of attack or bites or causes bodily injury to any person or animal; or

2. Any dog or other animal, while on the owner's property and in the absence of intentional provocation, bites or causes bodily injury to any person or animal lawfully on the property.

B. Quarantine For Dogs Or Other Animals Biting Persons Or Animals:

1. Every dog or other animal which bites a person or animal shall be promptly reported to law enforcement and the Prairie County public health department.

2. Any dog or other animal which has bitten any person or animal shall be kept under quarantine under the direction and authority of the Prairie County health officer at an animal shelter, veterinary facility, or other adequate facility. Such quarantine shall be for a period of ten (10) days.

3. If the owner of the dog or other animal has not appeared to claim the dog or other animal within five (5) days of the beginning of such quarantine, the dog or other animal may be destroyed pursuant to subsection 5-5-13C1 of this chapter and examined for rabies.
4. If, during the quarantine period, the dog or other animal is adjudged as having rabies, the dog or other animal shall be destroyed and appropriate health authorities notified.

5. If, after completion of the quarantine period, the dog or other animal is adjudged free of rabies, the dog or other animal shall be released to its owner upon written permission of the Prairie County health officer unless otherwise ordered held pursuant to subsection 5-5-13B of this chapter.

6. Quarantine and associated costs, including costs of destruction, shall be at the owner’s expense.

7. No person shall fail or refuse to surrender any dog or other animal for quarantine or destruction as required herein when demand is made by any law enforcement officer or the Prairie County health officer.

C. Disposition Of Dogs Or Other Animals Biting Or Causing Bodily Injury To Persons Or Animals: Any dog or other animal, under the circumstances set forth in this section, which bites or causes bodily injury to any person or animal on three (3) separate occasions, or bites or causes serious bodily injury to any person or animal on one occasion, may be put to death by any law enforcement officer in a humane manner or removed from the town pursuant to subsection 5-5-13C2 of this chapter. Provided, however, that if any vicious dog or other animal is found running at large and cannot be safely taken up and impounded, such vicious dog or other animal may be slain by any law enforcement officer. (Ord. 2015-06, 6-18-2015)

laws.title: Investigation
laws.content:
A. For the purpose of enforcing the provisions of this chapter, any law enforcement officer is empowered to demand from the occupants of any premises, upon or in which a dog or other animal is kept or harbored, the exhibition of such dog or other animal, and the license or tag for the animal. (1976 Code § 8.04.090; amd. 2016 Code)

B. Whenever complaint has been made that an animal is kept in a reportedly cruel or inhumane manner, the law enforcement officer may examine such animal and take possession of the same when, in his opinion, it requires humane treatment. (1976 Code § 8.04.090)

laws.title: Interference with LAW Enforcement Officer
laws.content: It is unlawful for any person to prevent, hinder or detain any law enforcement officer in the performance of any duty or power imposed on such officer by this chapter, or to release, or attempt to release any animal in the custody of any town official. (1976 Code § 8.04.100; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: Dogs Running at Large
laws.content: No owner or keeper of any dog shall permit such dog to run at large at any time within the corporate limits of the town, whether such dog be registered or unregistered. (1976 Code § 8.04.120)

laws.title: Animals Exposed to Rabies
laws.content:
A. Seizure; Quarantine: Every dog or other animal which has been bitten by, or exposed to, any animal suspected to have been infected with rabies shall be forthwith seized and taken up by any law enforcement officer and securely and separately impounded. All such animals shall be quarantined in the pound or at a licensed veterinarian hospital for a period of fourteen (14) days. It shall be the duty of the person seizing such dog to notify the Prairie County health officer of every such animal impounded.

B. Reclamation Of Animal Or Disposal: If, after observation under the supervision of the Prairie County health officer for such period, any such animal is adjudged free of rabies, the owner may reclaim the animal, upon payment of the regular keeping fees and upon compliance with the licensing diagnosed as being rabid, it shall be disposed of only under the orders and directions of the Prairie County health officer in his absolute discretion. (1976 Code § 8.04.130; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: Impoundment, Redemption and Disposition of Animals
laws.content:
A. Impoundment; Registry: Any law enforcement officer shall have the authority to apprehend any dog found running at large contrary to the provisions of this chapter and to impound such dog. The officer shall, upon receiving any dog, make a complete registry, entering the breed, color, and sex of such dog and the number of the registration tag if known.

B. Notice To Owner And Redemption: Not later than two (2) days after the impounding of any dog, the owner shall be notified in writing, or if the owner of the dog is unknown, written notice shall be posted for four (4) days at three (3) or more conspicuous places in the town, describing the dog and the place and time of taking. The owner of any dog so impounded may reclaim such dog upon proof of compliance with rabies vaccination provisions as herein provided, and upon payment of all costs and charges incurred by the town for impounding and maintenance of such dog, and upon purchasing a license for said impounded dog if that dog has not been licensed prior to capture.

C. Disposition Of Unclaimed Or Infected Dogs; Removal From Town:

1. It shall be the duty of any law enforcement officer to keep all dogs so impounded for a period of four (4) days. If at the expiration of four (4) days from the date of notice to the owner of the posting of notice, such dog shall not have been redeemed, it may be destroyed in a humane manner or sold. Any unregistered dog required by law to be registered, or any dog which appears to be suffering from rabies or affected with hydrophobia, mange, or other infectious or dangerous disease shall not be released, but may be forthwith destroyed in a humane manner. (1976 Code § 8.04.140; amd. 2016 Code)

2. Whenever an animal is to be put to death under this chapter, except for infection with rabies, the owner or other person may apply to law enforcement for permission to remove the animal permanently from the town. Upon such person’s filing with the court his written agreement to remove the animal from the town and be responsible for its remaining out permanently, the police judge may, in his discretion, make an order allowing the animal to be removed from the town instead of being put to death. (1976 Code § 8.08.040; amd. 2016 Code)

D. Teasing Or Unauthorized Release of Animals: It shall be unlawful for any person to tease, harass, or bother by any means, any dog which is upon the premises of the owner thereof. It shall further be unlawful for any person to release any dog from the premises of the owner, or to, in any manner, or by any means, lure such dog from the premises of the owner of the property, vehicle, or
enclosure in which such dog is contained. (1976 Code § 8.04.140)

laws.title: A. Animals Exposed To Rabies; Quarantine
laws.content:
1. Every dog or other animal which has been bitten by, or exposed to, any animal suspected to have been infected with rabies shall be forthwith seized and taken up by the chief of police or any law enforcement officer and securely and separately impounded in the town animal shelter. Such animal shall be quarantined in the pound or at a licensed veterinarian hospital for a period of fourteen (14) days. If after observation for such period, any such animal is adjudged free of rabies, the owner may reclaim the animal upon the payment of the regular keeping fees. In the event that any animal under quarantine or other confinement is diagnosed as being rabid, it shall be disposed of only under the orders and directions of a law enforcement officer in his absolute discretion. (1976 Code § 8.12.010; amd. 2016 Code)

2. No person shall delay or obstruct any town officer in the enforcement of this section. (1976 Code § 8.12.010)

laws.title: B. Vaccination
laws.content:
1. Whenever the town council, acting through its proper officer, shall deem it necessary to take extra measures to prevent the spread of the disease known as "rabies", the council shall designate a licensed veterinarian to vaccinate all dogs in the town with the proper vaccine. The cost of the vaccination shall be paid by the owner of the dog at the time of vaccination. Upon vaccination of such dog, the veterinarian shall issue to the owner his certificate showing the inoculation thereof. He shall keep a duplicate of such certificate and file the same in the office of the town clerk. A metallic tag may be attached to a collar on the dog showing the vaccination and the date thereof.

2. Whenever the town shall require the vaccination of dogs, no person shall obstruct or prevent an officer of the town from carrying out the duties required by subsection A of this section. (1976 Code § 8.12.020)

laws.title: Penalty
laws.content: Any owner or any other person found violating any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished as provided in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 8.04.150; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: Running at Large
laws.content: It shall be unlawful for any person to permit or allow any livestock or fowl belonging to him, or under his control, to run or roam at large in any of the streets, alleys, avenues, boulevards, parks or public places, or to trespass upon the premises of another person, within the corporate limits of the town. (Ord., 4-14-2009)

laws.title: Swine
laws.content: No person shall keep swine in the town. Swine may not be brought within the limits of the town except for marketing purposes. (1976 Code § 8.04.030)

laws.title: Keeping Livestock and Fowl
laws.content:
A. Keeping In Certain Area: No person owning, possessing or having control of any livestock or fowl shall permit or allow the
keeping of the same within the corporate limits of the town south of the Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railroad, except under the conditions as provided in subsection B of this section.

B. Conditions For Keeping:

1. Marketing Or Exhibition: Any person owning or having control of any livestock or fowl may bring the same into the corporate limits of the town for the purpose of marketing said livestock or for commercial or exhibition purpose, provided said livestock remains within the town fewer than seven (7) days per year. Exhibition purposes include parades or shows.

2. Visitors: It shall be permissible for any person owning or having control of any livestock or fowl to remove said animals from trucks or trailers for the purpose of exercising, feeding or watering the animals while the animals are en route from one location to another, provided the animals are not allowed to run at large, the owner cleans up any manure, bedding or feed products resulting from these operations, and said animals remain within the corporate limits less than twenty four (24) hours during any month.

3. Open Space: It shall be permissible for any person owning or having control of livestock or fowl to keep said animals within the corporate limits of the town south of the Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railroad for a limited time on property that provides adequate open space. The following conditions shall determine whether a property has adequate open space:

    a. Livestock and fowl shall be kept in low concentrations or on a short term basis so that manure does not accumulate and the animals do not generate odors offensive to neighboring properties. For the purposes of this article, no livestock or fowl shall be allowed on an area less than one acre in size, unless a special permit is granted under section 5-5A-5 of this article.

    b. All accessory structures used for the purpose of housing, keeping or sheltering livestock or fowl shall be set back a distance of fifty feet (50') from any property line, unless a variance is granted by the town council.

    c. All haystacks or feed storage bins shall be set back a distance of fifty feet (50') from any property line and fifty feet (50') from any dwelling or fire hazard. No haystack shall be carried over for more than two (2) years.

    d. The open space exception does not apply to swine, or vicious or ferocious animals, or to any areas where more restrictive covenants or zoning restrictions apply, or where other ordinances of the town apply.

    e. No owner of livestock or fowl shall be permitted to house, keep or shelter more than twenty (20) chickens, ducks, geese, turkeys and/or rabbits combined on a property within the corporate limits of the town south of the Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railroad. (Ord., 4-14-2009)

5-5A-5: PERMIT REQUIRED:

A. Permit: Any owner or keeper of livestock who desires to keep livestock within the corporate limits of the town south of the Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railroad using the open space exemption of subsection 5-5A-4B3 of this article must obtain a yearly (calendar year) permit from the town council.

B. Application For Permit: Application must be made in writing, with a description of the property on which the animal is to be kept, a description of fencing and other measures to contain the livestock or fowl and protect the public, and the length of time the animal is to be kept there. The owner or keeper of the livestock shall state and describe in the application any past health or safety concerns of the animal or fowl.

C. Special Permits: At its discretion, the council may issue special permits for the keeping of animals on parcels less than one acre in size. Special permits would be available only for animals being kept for short durations in a manner that assures adequate forage, cleanliness and odor control, or for small animals such as rabbits that can be kept in cages that are located in a manner that is not offensive to neighboring properties. (Ord., 4-14-2009)

5-5A-6: CAUSING ANNOYANCE, DISTURBANCE OR OFFENSE:

It shall be unlawful and a nuisance for any person owning or in control of any livestock or fowl to harbor or keep any livestock or fowl which causes annoyance or disturbance to residents of the town by loud and frequent noises such as baying, mooing, bleating, clucking, crowing, honking, or other noises. It shall also be unlawful and a nuisance to harbor or keep livestock or fowl in any manner which causes odors that are annoying, disturbing or offensive to the residents of the town. (Ord., 4-14-2009)

5-5A-7: VICIOUS, FEROCIOUS ANIMALS:

It shall be unlawful and a nuisance for any person to keep, feed or harbor or allow to stay about the premises occupied by him within the town, any vicious, unruly or ferocious animal. (Ord., 4-14-2009)

5-5A-8: PEST AND WEED CONTROL:

It shall be unlawful for any person keeping or harboring livestock or fowl within the town to fail to control flies, mice, rats or other pests, or to fail to control noxious weeds on the property where the livestock or fowl are kept. (Ord., 4-14-2009)

5-5A-9: DUTIES OF LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER:

A. Seizure Of Animal: It shall be the duty of the law enforcement officer to take up or cause to be taken up any livestock or fowl found to be loose or running at large or being kept unlawfully within the town. Upon impounding an animal, the officer shall notify the owner or keeper, if known, within a reasonable time that said animal has been impounded. The owner of any animal so impounded may reclaim such animal upon proof of compliance with section 5-5A-4 of this article and upon payment of all costs and charges incurred by the town for impounding and maintenance of such animal.

B. Notice Of Impoundment; Redemption; Disposition: It shall be the duty of the law enforcement officer to give notice of impoundment of any livestock by causing personal service on the owner, or some responsible person at the owner's residence or place of business. If such person cannot be found, notice shall be given by detention of the animal and by posting the information of impoundment in two (2) separate places in the town. The owner must redeem the impounded livestock within five (5) days after the giving of notice or it shall be subject to disposal or sale. Either the refusal or the failure of the owner to claim any such impounded livestock and to pay all costs and charges incurred by the town for impounding and maintenance of such animal shall be held to be an abandonment of the livestock by the owner. The law enforcement officer may offer the livestock for sale. In the event that any
impounded livestock is not redeemed by the owner or purchased, it may be disposed of by the law enforcement officer in a humane manner. (Ord., 4-14-2009; amd. 2016 Code)

**5-5A-10: FREEING ANIMALS FOR PURPOSE OF IMPOUNDMENT:**

No person shall disturb, take, or drive any animal or fowl out of any enclosure, stable or other building, or from outside of the town limits into the town, with the intent that such animal shall be impounded. (Ord., 4-14-2009)

**5-5A-11: AREA OF EXEMPTION:**

That portion of the town located north of the Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railroad is specifically exempt from section 5-5A-4 of this article because of the historical use of that portion of the town for the keeping of livestock and because a portion of the town located north of the railroad is still used only for agricultural purposes. (Ord., 4-14-2009)

**5-5A-12: EFFECT OF ARTICLE:**

This article shall not affect livestock being kept south of the Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railroad in the town on the effective date hereof. No new or replacement livestock may be kept or introduced after the effective date hereof without a permit required under section 5-5A-5 of this article. Offspring of livestock kept south of the Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railroad in the town on the effective date hereof may be kept without a permit required under section 5-5A-5 of this article only until they are old enough to be relocated to a site conforming to this section or outside of the town limits. (Ord., 4-14-2009)

**5-5A-13: PENALTIES:**

Conviction or a plea of "guilty" for a first offense for a violation of this article shall result in a thirty (30) day notice to clean up the property and if the property is not cleaned up in thirty (30) days, the permit will be revoked. If the town has to clean up the property, the cost of the cleanup will be assessed on the property owner's taxes. If the property owner cleans up the property, he or she may reapply for a permit to keep livestock. Failure to apply for a permit shall result in a thirty (30) day notice to apply. If application is not made by the end of the thirty (30) day period, conviction or a plea of "guilty", for harboring livestock or fowl without a permit shall result in a fine of twenty five dollars ($25.00). Conviction or a plea of "guilty" to a second offense to a violation of the provisions of this article shall result in a fine of fifty dollars ($50.00). Any owner or keeper of an animal convicted of, or pleading "guilty" to, a third or subsequent offense of the provisions of this article shall be punished by a fine of not to exceed five hundred dollars ($500.00). Payment of such fine does not relieve the owner or keeper of the animal from his duty to comply with the provisions of this article. (Ord., 4-14-2009)

laws.title: U-turns
Pedestrians Subject to Traffic Regulations
laws.content: At intersections or other areas where traffic control signals are in place, pedestrians shall be subject to such signals. At all other places, pedestrians shall be accorded the privileges and shall be subject to the restrictions stated in this title. (1976 Code § 10.12.010)

laws.title: Operation of Motorized Nonstandard Vehicles
laws.content:
A. Definition: A motorized nonstandard vehicle is a vehicle upon which a person may be transported that:

1. Is propelled by its own power;
2. Has a wheelbase of less than forty inches (40") and a wheel diameter of less than ten inches (10"); and
3. Does not display a certification in accordance with federal safety guidelines, or have a seventeen (17) digit VIN assigned by a manufacturer in accordance with federal guidelines.

B. Operation Authorized: The operation of a motorized nonstandard vehicle on the ways of this state open to the public located within the town of Terry is specifically authorized. (Ord., 6-8-2010)

laws.title: Enforcement of Traffic Regulations
laws.content:
A. Procedure Upon Arrest: 1. Except when authorized or directed under state law to immediately take a person arrested for a violation of any traffic law before a magistrate, any law enforcement officer, upon making an arrest for violation of the traffic ordinances of the town, shall take the name, address and operator’s license number of the alleged violator and license plate number of the motor vehicle involved and shall issue to him in writing a notice to answer to the charge against him at a place and at a time at least forty eight (48) hours after such arrest to be specified in the notice. (1976 Code § 10.32.010; amd. 2016 Code) 2. The officer, upon receiving the written promise of the alleged violator to answer as specified in the notice, shall release such person from custody. (1976 Code § 10.32.010) B. Failure To Obey Notice A Misdemeanor: 1. Any person who violates his written promise to appear, given to an officer upon an arrest for any alleged traffic violation, is guilty of a misdemeanor regardless of the disposition of the charge of which he was originally arrested. 2. Upon such failure to appear, a complaint may be entered against such person and a warrant of arrest issued. (1976 Code § 10.32.020) C. Notice On Illegally Parked Vehicle: 1. Whenever any motor vehicle without a driver is found parked or stopped in violation of any of the restrictions imposed by this traffic code or other ordinance of the town, the officer finding such vehicle shall take its registration number and may take any other information displayed on the vehicle which may identify its user, and shall conspicuously affix to such vehicle a notice in writing for the driver to answer to the charge against him within a specified time at least forty eight (48) hours later, during the hours and at a place specified in the notice. 2. The officer shall send one copy of such notice to the town court. (1976 Code § 10.32.030; amd. 2016 Code) D. Failure To Comply With Notice: 1. If a user of a motor vehicle charged with the violation of any restriction on stopping, standing, or parking under this traffic code does not appear in response to a notice affixed to such motor vehicle within the time specified in the notice, the proper law enforcement officer shall send to the owner of the motor vehicle to which the notice was affixed a letter informing him of the violation and requiring him or the aforesaid user of the vehicle to appear and answer the charge specified in the notice. The letter shall declare that in the event such letter is disregarded for a period of five (5) days, a complaint will be filed and warrant of arrest issued. (1976 Code § 10.32.040; amd. 2016 Code) 2. The failure of the owner or the said user of the vehicle to appear and answer within five (5) days of receipt of the letter shall constitute a misdemeanor, regardless of the disposition of the original charges. (1976 Code § 10.32.040) E. Authority To Impound Vehicles: 1. Law enforcement officers are hereby authorized to remove a vehicle from a street, highway or public parking lot to the nearest garage or other place of safety, or to a garage designated or maintained by the town under the circumstances hereinafter enumerated: a. When any vehicle is left unattended where such vehicle constitutes an obstruction to traffic. (1976 Code § 10.32.050; amd. 2016 Code) b. When a vehicle upon a street or highway is so disabled as to constitute an obstruction to traffic and the person in charge of the vehicle are, by reason of physical injury, incapacitated to such an extent as to be unable to provide for its custody or removal. c. When any vehicle is left unattended upon a street or highway and is so parked illegally as to constitute a definite hazard or obstruction to the normal movement of traffic. d. When any vehicle is parked illegally in a parking meter zone for an interval of more than six (6) hours. 2. Whenever an officer removes a vehicle from a street or other locality as authorized in this section and the officer knows or is able to ascertain from the registration records in the vehicle, the name and address of the owner thereof, the officer shall, within a reasonable time, make every reasonable effort to ascertain the identity of and to locate the owner of the vehicle and to give, or cause to be given, notice in writing to the owner of the fact of such removal and the reasons therefor and of the place to which said vehicle has been removed. In the event any such vehicle is stored in a public garage, a copy of such notice shall be given to the proprietor of such garage. 3. Whenever an officer removes a vehicle from a street or other locality under authority of this section and does not know and is not able to ascertain the name of the owner, or for any other reason is unable to give the notice to the owner as hereinbefore required, and in the event the vehicle is not returned to the owner within a period of three (3) days, then and in that event the officer shall immediately send, or cause to be sent, written report of such removal by mail to the state department of justice whose duty it is to register motor vehicles, and shall file a copy of such notice with the proprietor of any public garage in which the vehicle may be stored. Such notice shall include a complete description of the vehicle, the date, time, and place from which removed, the reasons for such removal, and name of the garage or place where the vehicle is stored. 4. Before the owner or person entitled to possession of any vehicle removed and impounded as provided herein shall be permitted to remove the same from the custody of the town, he shall furnish evidence of his identity and ownership of the vehicle, or right of possession thereto, shall sign a receipt for the vehicle, and shall pay any towing charges incurred by the town in towing said vehicle, and shall pay such charges for the storage of the vehicle as shall have been incurred by the town. 5. The payment of such fees and charges, as provided herein, shall not operate to relieve the owner or operator of such vehicle from liability from any fine or penalty for the violation of any law or ordinance on account of which such vehicle was removed and impounded. 6. Any vehicle left or parked on any street for five (5) consecutive days or longer shall be removed and sold in accordance with Montana Code Annotated sections 61-8-356, 61-12-401, and 61-12-408. (1976 Code § 10.32.050) 6-1-8: INSTALLATION OF TRAFFIC CONTROL SIGNS, SIGNALS AND DEVICES: The director of public works or local law enforcement, under the direction of the town council, shall place and maintain traffic control signs, signals and devices, conforming to the state manual and specifications, upon town streets, except state highways, when and as required under the traffic ordinances, and may place and maintain such additional traffic control devices as they or the town council may deem necessary to regulate traffic under the traffic ordinances of the town or under state law, or to warn or guide traffic. (Ord. 2015-07, 8-12-2015) 6-1-9: PENALTY: Any person violating a provision of this chapter for which another penalty has not been provided shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 10.04.050)

CHAPTER 2

PARKING REGULATIONS

SECTION: 6-2-1: Parking On Private Property 6-2-2: Obstructing Traffic 6-2-3: Parking In Alleys 6-2-4: Parking For Certain Purposes Prohibited 6-2-5: Parking Restricted In Certain Areas 6-2-6: Parking Vehicles For Transport Of Flammable Liquids 6-2-7: Penalty

laws.title: Parking on Private Property
laws.content:
A. Consent Required: No person shall stand or park a vehicle on any private lot or lot area without the express or implied consent of the owner thereof.

B. Compliance With Signs: Whenever signs or markings have been erected on any lot or lot area, contiguous or adjacent to a street, thoroughfare, or alley, indicating that no vehicles are permitted to stand or park thereon, it shall be unlawful for any person to drive a vehicle across any curb or lot line or over any driveway from a street or alley into said lot or area for the purpose of standing or parking such vehicle, or, for any person to stop, stand, or park any vehicle in such lot or lot area. (1976 Code § 10.08.010)

laws.title: Obstructing Traffic
laws.content: No person shall park any vehicle upon a street, other than an alley, in such a manner or under such conditions as to leave available less than ten feet (10') of the width of the roadway for free movement of vehicular traffic. (1976 Code § 10.08.020)

laws.title: Parking in Alleys
laws.content:
A. No person shall stop, stand, or park any vehicle, whether occupied or not, within any alley in the business district at any time otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading.

B. No person shall stop, stand or park any vehicle, whether occupied or not, within any alley in the town in such a manner as to prevent the free movement of vehicular traffic or in such a position as to block the driving entrance to any abutting property, except when engaged in loading or unloading. (1976 Code § 10.08.030)

laws.title: Parking for Certain Purposes Prohibited
Parking Restricted in Certain Areas
laws.content:
A. The parking of motor vehicles on particular streets or parts of streets within the town is controlled by the regulations of this chapter and other ordinances of the town.

B. When appropriate signs are erected, giving indication of such regulations, no driver of a vehicle shall disobey the direction of any such sign. (1976 Code § 10.44.010)

laws.title: Parking Vehicles for Transport of Flammable Liquids
laws.content: No tank, truck, trailer or like vehicle containing, or used for the transportation of, gasoline, butane, fuel oil or other highly flammable liquid shall be parked on any street, alley, public park or other public place, nor upon any private property in the town for a period longer than one hour. Provided, that this restriction upon parking shall not be construed as to prevent the delivery of such liquids to retail gas stations or to private residences or business property for so long a period as is reasonably necessary. (1976 Code § 10.08.050)

laws.title: Penalty
laws.content: Any person violating a provision of this chapter for which another penalty has not been provided shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 10.08.140)

laws.title: Authority to Weigh Trucks
laws.content: The law enforcement officer shall have the authority to require any person driving or in control of any truck not proceeding over a truck route or street over which truck traffic is permitted to proceed to any public or private scale available for the purpose of weighing and determining compliance with this chapter. (Ord. 2014-05, 10-9-2014; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: Truck Routes
laws.content:
A. Designation: There are established within the town the following truck routes:

1. North Entry:

   a. Trucks entering the town from the north on Highway 253 shall enter the town limits using: 1) Montague Avenue; 2) Laundre Avenue; or 3) Spring Street.

   b. Trucks entering the town from the north on Fair Grounds Road or Hoagland Street shall enter the town limits using: 1) Montague Avenue; 2) Laundre Avenue; or 3) Spring Street.

2. South Entry: Trucks entering the town from the south on Ten Mile Road or Highway 253 shall enter the town limits using: a) Spring Street; b) Laundre Avenue; or c) Montague Avenue.

3. East Entry: Trucks entering the town from the east on Old Highway 10 shall enter the town limits using: a) Spring Street; b) Laundre Avenue; or c) Montague Avenue.

4. West Entry: Trucks entering the town from the west on Old Highway 10 or Cemetery Loop Road shall enter the town limits using: a) Spring Street; b) Laundre Avenue; or c) Montague Avenue.

B. Maps: The town clerk shall keep and maintain accurate maps setting out truck routes and streets upon which truck traffic is permitted. The maps shall be kept on file in the office of the town clerk and shall be available to the public. (Ord. 2014-05, 10-9-2014)

laws.title: USE Generally
laws.content:
A. All trucks traveling within the town shall be operated only over and along the truck routes and other permissible streets established by this chapter.

B. Truckers utilizing the town streets shall do so in such manner as to travel the most practicable route to their destination within the town. (Ord. 2014-05, 10-9-2014)

laws.title: Exceptions
laws.content:
This chapter shall not prohibit:

A. Street Necessary For Destination: The operation of trucks upon any street that is necessary to gain access to a destination point for the purpose of transacting business; provided, that streets designated as truck routes are used until reaching the intersection nearest the destination necessitating departure from the truck route.

B. Street Necessary For Departure: The operation of trucks upon any street that is necessary to gain access to a particular truck route from a point of departure; provided, that the most direct course providing such access is followed.

C. Emergency Vehicles: The operation of emergency vehicles upon any street in the town.

D. Town Public Utilities Or Street Repair Vehicles: The operation of trucks owned or operated by the town or public utilities or any contractor or subcontractor while engaged in the repair, maintenance, construction or improvement of streets or street utilities within the town.

E. Detoured Trucks: The operation of trucks over streets designated as a lawfully established detour.

F. Agricultural Trucks: The operation of agricultural or stock trucks which are not loaded and are being used at the time for the sole purpose of passenger transportation to the place of residence of the driver or owner, provided such vehicle emits no noxious or offensive odors. (Ord. 2014-05, 10-9-2014)

laws.title: Penalty
laws.content:
Any person who violates the provisions of this chapter shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punishable by a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100.00) and not more than five hundred dollars ($500.00). (Ord. 2014-05, 10-9-2014)
**CHAPTER 4** **BICYCLES AND MOTORCYCLES**
SECTION: 6-4-1: Bicycles 6-4-2: Motorcycles 6-4-3: Penalty

laws.title: Bicycles
laws.content:
A. Dismounting To Make Turn: Whenever authorized signs are erected indicating that no right or left or U-turn is permitted, no person operating a bicycle shall disobey the direction of any such sign, except where such person dismounts from the bicycle to make any such turn, in which event he shall then obey the regulations applicable to pedestrians. (1976 Code § 10.16.010)

B. Manner Of Riding:

1. A person propelling a bicycle shall not ride other than astride a permanent and regular seat attached thereto.

2. No bicycle shall be used to carry more persons at one time than the number for which it is designed and equipped. (1976 Code § 10.16.020)

C. Parking: No person shall park a bicycle upon a street other than upon the roadway against the curb or upon the sidewalk in a rack to support the bicycle or against a building, in such manner as to afford the least obstruction to pedestrian traffic. No person shall park a bicycle against a glass window at any time. (1976 Code § 10.16.030)

D. Riding On Sidewalks: Whenever any person is riding a bicycle upon a sidewalk, such person shall yield the right of way to any pedestrian and shall give audible signal before overtaking and passing such pedestrian. (1976 Code § 10.16.040; amd. 2016 Code)

E. Lamps And Other Equipment:

1. Every bicycle when in use at nighttime shall be equipped with a lamp on the front which shall emit a white light visible from a distance of at least five hundred feet (500') to the front. A lamp emitting a red light visible from a distance of five hundred feet (500') to the rear may be used in addition to rear facing reflectors required by this section.

2. Every bicycle when in use at nighttime shall be equipped with an essentially colorless front facing reflector, essentially colorless or amber pedal reflectors, and a red rear facing reflector. Pedal reflectors shall be mounted on the front and back of each pedal.

3. Every bicycle when in use at nighttime shall be equipped with either tires with retroreflective sidewalls or reflectors mounted on the spokes of each wheel. Spoke mounted reflectors shall be within seventy six millimeters (76 mm) (3.0 in) of the inside of the rim and shall be visible on each side of the wheel. The reflectors on the front wheel shall be essentially colorless or amber and the reflectors on the rear wheel shall be amber or red.

4. Reflectors required by this subsection E shall be of a type approved by the state division of motor vehicles. (1976 Code § 10.16.050)

5. Every bicycle shall be equipped with a brake which will enable the operator to make the braked wheels skid on dry, level, clean pavement. (2016 Code)

6. Bicycle owners are encouraged to have their bicycles equipped with a flag clearly visible from the rear and suspended not less than six feet (6') above the roadway when the bicycle is standing upright. The flag shall be fluorescent orange in color. (1976 Code § 10.16.050)

laws.title: Motorcycles
laws.content:
A. Motor Driven Cycles: The term "motorcycles" when used in this section, shall include motor driven cycles. (1976 Code § 10.16.210)

B. General Traffic Laws Apply: Every person riding a motorcycle upon a street or roadway shall be granted all of the rights and shall be subject to all of the duties applicable to the driver of a vehicle by the provisions of this traffic code and other traffic ordinances of the town, except as to special regulations in this chapter and except as to those provisions of laws which, by their nature, can have no such application. (1976 Code § 10.16.220)

laws.title: Penalty
laws.content: Any person violating a provision of this chapter for which another penalty has not been provided shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 10.16.230)

laws.title: Effect of Regulations
laws.content:
A. It is a violation of this chapter for any person to do any act forbidden or fail to perform any act required by this chapter.

B. The parent of any child and the guardian of any ward shall not authorize or knowingly permit any such child or ward to violate any of the provisions of this chapter.

C. These regulations applicable to snowmobiles shall apply whenever a snowmobile is operated upon any street, or upon any public path set aside for the exclusive use of snowmobiles, subject to those exceptions stated herein. (1976 Code § 10.50.020)

laws.title: State Registration Required
laws.content: The owner of a snowmobile shall register such vehicle at the county treasurer’s office in the county where the owner resides and shall further comply with all provisions of Montana Code Annotated section 23-2-616. The owner shall display in a conspicuous place on such registered vehicle, the registered number. (1976 Code § 10.50.030; amd. 2016 Code)

laws.title: Operation Generally
laws.content:
A. Controlled Access Highway: No person shall operate a snowmobile upon a controlled access highway or facility.

B. Crossing Street Or Highway: A snowmobile may make a direct crossing of a street or highway, where such crossing is necessary to get to another authorized area of operation. Such crossings shall be made at an angle of approximately ninety degrees (90°) to the direction of the highway, at a place where no obstruction prevents a quick and safe crossing. The snowmobile shall make a complete stop before entering upon any part of the highway or road and the operator shall yield the right of way to all oncoming traffic.

C. Equipment: No snowmobile shall be operated upon a public street or highway when permitted to do so by this chapter, unless equipped with a brake light, at least one headlamp and one taillamp, which shall be lighted at all times during such operation, and unless equipped with a suitable braking device which may be operated by either hand or foot. (1976 Code § 10.50.040)

laws.title: Unlawful Operation
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to drive or operate any snowmobile in any one or more of the following manners:

A. Violation Of State Or Local Laws: In violation of any statute of the state of Montana or ordinance of the town of Terry, regulating the operation of motor vehicles.

B. Careless Or Reckless Manner: In a careless or reckless manner so as to endanger the person or property of another, or to cause injury or damage to either.

C. Muffler: Without a muffler in good working order and in constant operation which prevents excessive or unusual noise and annoying smoke.

D. Pulling Sled Or Trailer: To pull any sled or trailer or any other object without a "rigid type" hitch. (1976 Code § 10.50.050)

laws.title: Operation on Private Property
laws.content: Snowmobiles shall not be operated on private property without the permission of the owner and at no time shall they be operated on sidewalks or posted areas. (1976 Code § 10.50.060)

laws.title: Riding on Streets, Roadways and Snowmobile Paths
laws.content:
A. Use Of Right Side Of Roadway: Every person operating a snowmobile upon a street or roadway shall ride as near to the right hand side of the roadway as practicable, exercising due care when passing a standing vehicle or one proceeding in the same direction. B. Riding Single File: Persons riding snowmobiles upon a street or roadway shall not ride more than single file except on paths or parts of roadways set aside for the exclusive use of snowmobiles. (1976 Code § 10.50.070) **6-5-8: EMERGING FROM ALLEYS, DRIVEWAYS AND BUILDINGS:** In emerging from alleys, driveways, or buildings, snowmobile operators shall, upon approaching a sidewalk or the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway, yield the right of way to all pedestrians approaching on said sidewalk or sidewalk area, and, upon entering the roadway, shall yield the right of way to all vehicles approaching on said roadway. (1976 Code § 10.50.080) **6-5-9: CLINGING TO VEHICLES PROHIBITED:** No person riding upon any snowmobile shall attach the same or himself to any vehicle upon the street or roadway. (1976 Code § 10.50.090) **6-5-10: PARKING:** No person shall park a snowmobile upon a street other than upon the roadway against the curb or upon the sidewalk in such a manner as to afford the least obstruction to pedestrian traffic. (1976 Code § 10.50.100) **6-5-11: RIDING ON SIDEWALKS:** No person shall ride a snowmobile upon any sidewalk. (1976 Code § 10.50.110) **6-5-12: PENALTY:** Violation of any section of this chapter, or any rule or regulation established hereunder, shall be a misdemeanor and punishable by fine or imprisonment, or both, as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 10.50.120; amd. 2016 Code)

TITLE 7

PUBLIC WAYS AND PROPERTY

CHAPTER 1

STREETS, SIDEWALKS AND PUBLIC WAYS

SECTION: 7-1-1: Materials Obstructing Streets 7-1-2: Signs, Fences And Other Structural Obstructions 7-1-3: Protection Of Streets And Traffic During Construction **7-1-1: MATERIALS OBSTRUCTING STREETS:** A. Permission Required: No person shall encumber or obstruct, or cause to be encumbered or obstructed, any street, alley or other public place in the town by placing therein or thereon any building materials, trash, vehicle, earth, garbage, rubbish, debris, or accumulated snow and ice removed from an adjoining private premises, without first having obtained permission in writing from the town clerk, or other responsible town official. (1976 Code § 12.12.010) B. Order To Remove: 1. An enforcement official or designee of the town council is authorized to order any article or thing, of the kind mentioned in subsection A of this section, which encumbers, litters or obstructs any street, alley or other public place within the town, to be removed. (1976 Code § 12.12.020; amd. 2016 Code) 2. If such removal shall not be made within six (6) hours after notice to the owner or person in charge thereof, or if the owner cannot be readily found for the purpose of such notice, the town shall cause the same to be removed to some suitable place to be designated by such official, at the expense of the person responsible thereof. (1976 Code § 12.12.020) **7-1-2: SIGNS, FENCES AND OTHER STRUCTURAL OBSTRUCTIONS:** A. Permit Required; Restrictions: 1. No person shall place or maintain any shafts of wood, iron or other material, billboards, signs, fences, poles, rods, cables, or wires in any of the streets, public places or alleys of the town without having first obtained a permit from the town council. 2. It shall be unlawful for any person, either as owner or occupant of any premises within the town, to erect, or cause to be erected, or to permit or suffer to remain any sign, marquee, eave, or other private structures, which project over any sidewalk or street adjoining any state or national highway through the town, unless the lowest portion thereof shall have a clearance from the top of the curb, sidewalk or highway shoulder elevation of not less than seven and one-half feet ( $7^{1/2}$ ), and a lateral clearance of at least three feet (3') behind the face of the curb, or sidewalk, or shoulder of the road, unless permission for the erection or maintenance thereof shall have first been secured from the town council. (1976 Code § 12.12.030) 3. Any person violating any of the provisions of this subsection A shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code; and in addition, the town shall have the right to remove any sign, marquee, eave or other private structure unlawfully erected if the same is not removed by the owner within five (5) days from the date of service of notice to remove given by any town officer. (1976 Code § 12.12.030; amd. 2016 Code) B. Structural Obstructions; Permit For Limited Time: 1. No person shall maintain any building, fence, porch, steps, gallery, or other structure upon any street or alley within the town. 2. The town council may, in its discretion, grant permits to persons which will allow them to maintain such structures for a limited time to be specified in the permit. (1976 Code § 12.12.040) C. Order To Remove: 1. Any building, fence, porch, steps, gallery, or other structural obstruction now upon or hereafter placed or erected upon any street or alley within the town, or which may be upon any new street or alley which may hereafter be opened or created within the town, shall be removed therefrom within a reasonable time, not exceeding thirty (30) days and not less than three (3) days after an order to remove, in writing, has been given to the owner or person responsible for such obstruction. (1976 Code § 12.12.050) 2. If the owner or person responsible for such obstruction cannot be readily found for the purpose of such notice, it shall be the duty of an enforcement official or designee of the town council to cause the obstruction to be removed, in his discretion. The expense of such removal shall be recoverable from the owner or person responsible for the obstruction. (1976 Code § 12.12.050; amd. 2016 Code) 3. Any person who interferes with, resists or obstructs by acts or threats, the removal of any such obstruction shall be deemed guilty of a violation of this chapter. (1976 Code § 12.12.050) D. Order To Remove Obstructions: Notice to remove obstructions described in subsections A and C of this section, specifying same, and the place and extent of same, shall be given to the occupant or owner of the land involved, or to the person owning or causing such obstruction. Notice shall be given by leaving such notice at the place of residence of the person to be served, if he resides in the town, or by posting such notice on the obstruction, if such person does not reside in the town. (1976 Code § 12.12.060) 7-1-3: PROTECTION OF STREETS AND TRAFFIC DURING CONSTRUCTION: A. Barricades And Warning Lights: 1. Whenever excavation work in any street in the town is in progress, efficient barricades shall be erected by the contractor, or other person in control, around all trenches or embankments made by him within the limits of any street or sidewalk. Red lights shall be maintained thereon from dusk to daylight until the street or sidewalk shall be restored to a safe and passable condition. 2. Failure or omission to protect against accident, in the manner required by this section, shall cause a forfeiture of any permit which may have been granted with reference thereto. 3. Following completion of the construction work and restoration of the street or sidewalk to a safe and passable condition, the contractor or person in charge of the work shall promptly remove all barricades, warning lights and other safety devices from the street or sidewalk. (1976 Code § 12.16.010) B. Traveling Upon Streets With Barricades: No person shall walk upon or drive upon a street, alley or sidewalk barricaded as stated in this section. (1976 Code § 12.16.020) C. Removal Of Barricades And Warning Devices Prohibited: Whenever any barricade, red light or other warning device shall have been placed upon the streets, alleys or sidewalks of the town in the course of his duty, or by any contractor working on any street, alley or sidewalk, no person shall move or remove such red light, barricade or other warning device. (1976 Code § 12.16.030) D. Marking Wet Concrete: Where lights, signs, barricades or obstructions have been placed and maintained to protect concrete, no person shall walk, run, drive, ride or step upon the newly laid concrete, so as to mark, mar, or in any way, injure the same. (1976 Code § 12.16.040) E. Chipping Concrete: No person other than an enforcement official or designee of the town council shall intentionally or wilfully chip, break, cut or in any manner, deface or injure any concrete in any sidewalk, curb, gutter or pavement. (1976 Code § 12.16.050; amd. 2016 Code) F. Penalty: Any person violating a provision of this section shall, upon conviction thereof, be punished by a fine as set forth in section 1-4-1 of this code. (1976 Code § 12.16.060; amd. 2016 Code) **CHAPTER 2** **EXCAVATIONS** SECTION: 7-2-1: Definitions 7-2-2: Permit; Bond; And Insurance Required 7-2-3: Surface And Subsurface Restoration Required 7-2-4: Minimum Travel Interference 7-2-5: Time Limit For Open Excavation 7-2-6: Backfilling 7-2-7: Protection Of Existing Utilities 7-2-8: Revocation Of Permit 7-2-9: Penalty 7-2-1: DEFINITIONS: For the purpose of this chapter, the following terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section: EXCAVATION: Shall mean and include any ditch, trench, cut, hole or change of grade. STREET: The entire width of a highway between the boundary lines of other public or private properties on the sides. (1976 Code § 12.04.010) 7-2-2: PERMIT; BOND; AND INSURANCE REQUIRED: A. Requirements: No person, association or corporation shall open up, dig into, excavate or tunnel in any of the streets, avenues, alleys or public places of the Town, whether to connect with any of the mains or pipes, to connect with any sewer, or for any other purpose, without having first: 1. Obtained a permit from the Town; 2. Posted with the Town Clerk a good and sufficient indemnity and performance security bond; and 3. Filed with the Town Clerk a certificate of insurance or its equivalent providing for public liability coverage. B. Permit: The fee for a permit required by subsection A1 of this section shall be ten dollars ($10.00). C. Bond: The indemnity and performance security bond required by subsection A2 of this section shall be not less than five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) payable to the Town, to protect the Town from any liability of any kind or character whatsoever, which may arise as a result of said permittee’s opening any street, avenue, alley or public place of the Town, or which may in any way or manner be connected therewith, or related thereto and to guaranty that the refilling, compacting and restoration of the surface and subsurface of the opened street, avenue, alley or public place is in accordance with specifications set forth in this chapter. D. Insurance: The insurance required by subsection A3 of this section shall be public liability coverage in the sum of not less than five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000.00) for each person, and an aggregate sum of one million dollars ($1,000,000.00) for more than one person on account of any one accident, and fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) for property damage, to protect the parties and indemnify, hold harmless, and defend the Town from any expense, cost, damage and any liability of any kind or character whatsoever resulting from or which may arise as a result of said permittee’s opening any such street, avenue, alley or public place, or which may in any way be connected therewith, or relating thereto. (Ord. 2017-03, 10-12-2017) 7-2-3: SURFACE AND SUBSURFACE RESTORATION REQUIRED: A. All persons, associations or corporations making excavations in any street, avenue, alley or public place of the Town shall be responsible for refilling and compacting in accordance with specifications set forth in this chapter and shall be responsible for surface and subsurface restoration within fourteen (14) days from the date of making said excavation, unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the Town. B. The party making excavation is responsible for all costs incurred in refilling, compacting, and surface and subsurface restoration. (Ord. 2017-03, 10-12-2017) 7-2-4: MINIMUM TRAVEL INTERFERENCE: Excavations in streets and alleys shall be made in such manner as to impede travel as little as possible. At no time during the progress of the work shall sidewalks be unnecessarily blocked to travel. (1976 Code § 12.04.050) 7-2-5: TIME LIMIT FOR OPEN EXCAVATION: The time that any street or alley excavation is open may be limited by an enforcement official or designee of the Town Council. (1976 Code § 12.04.060; amd. 2016 Code) 7-2-6: BACKFILLING: A. Restoration Of Street Surface: After the completing of the laying of any pipe, line or conduit, or the installation or repair of any facility for which the excavation was undertaken, the excavator shall cause the work to be backfilled in such a manner as to make the street in as good a condition as before the excavation. B. Maintenance: Any person making any excavation in any street or alley, as set forth in this chapter, shall be fully responsible for the maintenance of the excavation for a period of six (6) months after the backfill thereof.
